text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The caretaker cabinet approved an accountability bill to net corrupt politicians and civilian and military bureaucrats.

- The Lahore High Court has issued notice to the director general of paramilitary rangers on an amended petition seeking the court's direction on depositing 700 million rupees in the State (central) Bank of Pakistan. The money was recovered from Asif Ali Zardari, spouse of sacked prime minister Benazir Bhutto, at Governor House in Lahore on November 5.
- Pakistan has achieved a breakthrough in qualifying for enhanced assistance from the IMF as well as receiving $160 million on account of stalled $600 million standby loan.
- Chinese president Jiang Zemin will arrive Pakistan on December 1 on a five-day state visit.
- A nine-member caretaker cabinet of the North West Frontier Province was sworn in at Governor House.
- About 200 supporters of Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party staged a protest procession in Peshawar against the dissolution of the National Assembly.
- The caretaker government has told public sector corporations and financial institutions to terminate the services of all retired employees re-employed on contract.
- The government is expected to announce some relief from the additional taxes levied by the previous government to raise 13 billion rupees in the mini-budget.
- Pak-Arab Refinery has announced a dividend of 29 percent amounting to 626 million rupees for fiscal 1995/96.
- The Pakistani government has decided to end a 17-month-old ban on cellular telephone services in the southern province of Sindh, including its violence-prone capital Karachi.
- A Pakistani anti-terrorist court sentenced two men to death for a bomb blast at Lahore airport in July that killed four people and wounded nearly 70, court officials said.
